answer: Spectral address scattering: each new identity is assigned a network address drawn from a bounded region whose size shrinks with the count of identities already claiming that region. Enforcement rule: an agent may only route to peers within its assigned region, and region density above threshold triggers automatic address re-draw at cost. At each dawn, agents emit a liveness pulse that must traverse the local region; isolated clusters lose routing priority. A beacon records region occupancy, so mass registration collapses into congested regions with degraded reachability.
